tldr: A live ~7-month US-Iran war is the single biggest live risk to the book: Houthi missiles struck Saudi Arabia's Yanbu/Taif export infrastructure and Iran threatened to widen the conflict, sending Brent +3.27% to ~$106.45 and WTI +2.42% to ~$94.39 on 9/24 -- the IEA calls it the largest oil-supply disruption in market history -- even as reported US-Iran talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz capped the spike, making this a genuinely two-sided catalyst.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish surprise, hiking 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep with nine of eighteen officials eyeing another 2026 hike, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to ~5.0-5.1%, its highest since 2007 -- the single biggest structural headwind for the levered silver/gold-miners sleeve via a firmer dollar, while a genuine tailwind for the DBS/OCBC leg (Jefferies just initiated Buy on both).

Sentiment and breadth confirm a narrow, still-weakening market beneath a deceptively low VIX (~15.7): Fear&Greed ticked up only slightly to 36/Fear, under half of S&P names sit above their 200-/50-day averages, and the McClellan Oscillator remains deeply oversold.

China continues slow-walking rare-earth magnet export licenses (August US-bound shipments -21% month-on-month) even after Trump and Xi extended their trade truce to mid-January 2027 -- reinforcing the case for the Western rare-earth watchlist (MP, Lynas, USA Rare Earth) even as the truce caps near-term escalation risk.

regime.label: Hawkish-Fed war-shock: equities still pricing complacency
regime.oneLiner: A live Iran war has triggered the largest oil-supply disruption in market history just as a newly hawkish Fed pushed the 10-year yield to its highest since 2007, yet equities and the VIX remain oddly calm beneath a narrow, deteriorating breadth picture.

topNews.headline: Houthi missile barrage on Saudi Arabia and Iranian threat to widen war send Brent above $106
topNews.actionable: Escalation risk supports a safe-haven bid for gold/silver but the accompanying yield spike and risk-off tone are pressuring miners and broad equities simultaneously, so the net read for the book is ambiguous rather than a clean tailwind.

topNews.headline: US and Iran explore phased deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz, ease blockade
topNews.actionable: A credible de-escalation path caps further oil-driven safe-haven demand for metals and could reverse some of Thursday's flight-to-safety flow into gold/silver if talks progress over the weekend.

topNews.headline: Fed hikes rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% under new Chair Warsh, first hike since 2023, signals more to come
topNews.actionable: A hawkish, still-hiking Fed is the single biggest headwind for the silver/gold miners leg of the book via a stronger dollar and higher real yields, while it is a structural tailwind for the DBS/OCBC net-interest-margin story and a further drag on SGX REIT valuations.

topNews.headline: Gold and silver slide as dollar rallies on firming Fed hike bets
topNews.actionable: The dollar-driven pullback in gold/silver is the direct near-term risk to the levered silver and miner sleeve of the book; watch whether the metals decouple positively if Hormuz talks fail and the Iran war escalates further.

topNews.headline: China's rare-earth magnet exports to US plunge 21% ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
topNews.actionable: A deliberate squeeze on magnet exports even alongside a truce extension directly strengthens the investment case for the Western rare-earth watchlist (MP, Lynas, USA Rare Earth) as buyers scramble for non-China supply.

signals: MP Materials is the model's highest-conviction rare-earth call (pUp3m 0.60, confidence 0.55) on its DoD equity stake, $110/kg NdPr price floor and DoD-backed separation expansion -- consider watching for continuation independent of the broader miner-sector pullback.

SMH/XLK remain the model's steadiest near-term tech convictions (pUp3m 0.55-0.58, confidence 0.55) on the intact AI-capex supercycle (~$775-800B 2026 hyperscaler spend) -- consider watching for resilience even as the broader tape wobbles on rate/war risk.

GLD/SLV keep a double-digit 12-month expected return (ev12m 0.09/0.10) on record central-bank gold buying and a 5th-consecutive annual silver supply deficit, despite the near-term dollar-driven pullback -- consider watching whether this proves a buyable dip or a genuine cooldown.

Rare-earth dispersion is back in focus: Lynas and USA Rare Earth screen better than 6680.HK (JL Mag) given China's continued export-license slow-walking despite the Trump-Xi truce -- consider watching whether ex-China names keep outperforming the Chinese incumbent.

Congress and smart money are split rather than aligned on the AI trade (Whitehouse sold Nvidia, Burry's newsletter shorted both Nvidia and Palantir, while retail piles into IonQ and Meta) -- consider watching for whether this cools the AI-momentum trade broadly.
